attacks.claim: The plan never says whether existing paid-member subscriptions in the old membership plugin are cancelled, paused, or left running when Ghost imports the same Stripe customers. That risks double-billing or orphaning paying members.
attacks.evidence: "Paid members are matched to Stripe customers by Stripe customer ID (not email) using Ghost's Stripe import"; ABSENT: old-plugin subscription cancellation or cutover step

attacks.claim: Suppression is a single import-time snapshot. Opt-outs and bounces on MailPoet between the final Thursday send and the production import, and in Ghost after cutover, have no delta sync, so opted-out people can be re-mailed.
attacks.evidence: "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed (never as active), so nobody who opted out is re-mailed."; ABSENT: delta sync or import timing relative to the final MailPoet send

attacks.claim: Rollback covers only new email signups. Paid-member creation, cancellations, Stripe changes, and sends made from Ghost are not reconciled back to MailPoet, so rollback splits the member list and can re-mail people already reached by Ghost.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet"

attacks.claim: The seed gate has no measurement window, denominator, or failure action. At 2,000 addresses a 0.1% complaint threshold is about two complaints, and the remainder send fires automatically at 2 hours with no abort path.
attacks.evidence: "the remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%"

attacks.claim: The 37 mismatched paid members have no owner, deadline, audit trail, or interim access rule. The ~3,100 paying members outside the dry run are not checked against Stripe.
attacks.evidence: "37 members with mismatched emails were identified in a dry run and will be resolved by hand before cutover."

attacks.claim: The exit rehearsal uses 50 addresses through Postmark, not the production Mailgun path at 46k recipients, so the stated exit to another bulk sender is untested at real volume.
attacks.evidence: "we rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts"

attacks.claim: Ghost, MySQL, nightly dumps, and bulk sending share one 4 vCPU / 8 GB box, the same co-location that produced the four outages. No load test, concurrency limit, or isolation is shown.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box"; ABSENT: load test or isolation of bulk send from site traffic

attacks.claim: No alerting or named owner covers failed nightly dumps, failed weekly exports, stalled sends, or Mailgun errors, so a silent backup failure would surface only at restore time.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)"; ABSENT: alerting, backup verification, on-call owner

attacks.claim: The domain is warmed in week 2, then a 46k-address remainder goes out 2 hours after a 2,000-address seed. No volume ramp schedule or deliverability target is given, so full-volume deliverability is unproven.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun domain warm-up (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)" in week 2; "the remainder sends 2 hours later"

attacks.claim: No consent-basis review of migrated active subscribers and no Mailgun DPA are documented before a 46k send from a new sender. Reconciling totals does not verify that each subscriber's consent evidence supports the new flow.
attacks.evidence: "consent source/IP where recorded"; ABSENT: consent-basis review and Mailgun DPA; "counts reconciled against MailPoet totals"

attacks.claim: A 0.5 FTE developer must deliver the theme port, Stripe import, migration, redirects, DNS, and warm-up in 4 weeks with no buffer and no go/no-go criteria. Week 3 stacks the Stripe dry run on top of the final MailPoet send.
attacks.evidence: "Owner: dev (0.5 FTE) + managing editor | 4 weeks"; "Week 3: Stripe import dry run, reconciliation, editor training; final Thursday send on MailPoet."

attacks.claim: Consent IP addresses are carried into the primary Ghost database and into backups and weekly exports. The plan states no retention limit or erasure path for them.
attacks.evidence: "consent source/IP where recorded"

attacks.claim: Backup encryption key custody, key rotation, and object-storage access control are not specified, though dumps and exports contain member PII.
attacks.evidence: "nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)"

attacks.claim: Recipient data sent to Mailgun has no stated DPA, sub-processor list, or data residency, which bears on the claim that subscriber data stays under the publication's control.
attacks.evidence: "Mailgun only receives per-send recipient batches."

attacks.claim: The line items do not reconcile: $48 plus $90 leaves about $2 for storage, backups, and transactional SMTP, none of which is priced. The Mailgun tier is not named, so the estimate cannot be checked as volume grows.
attacks.evidence: "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today."; "Estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)."

attacks.claim: Weekly CSV and JSON exports accumulate in object storage with no stated retention, so storage cost is unbounded and absent from the run-cost total.
attacks.evidence: "members CSV export and JSON content export are scheduled weekly (cron, stored with the DB dumps)"

attacks.claim: There is no decommission or data-deletion step for the old VPS after the 30-day read-only window, so legacy personal data may persist with no owner.
attacks.evidence: "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days"; ABSENT: decommission plan

attacks.claim: The exit rehearsal covers newsletter sending only. Paid-membership and Stripe-linked state, which the plan treats as valuable, has no tested exit path.
attacks.evidence: "disable Ghost newsletter sending and load the weekly members export into another bulk sender"

attacks.claim: No upgrade cadence, staging test, or owner is named for Ghost, MySQL, or the Docker image on a single box maintained by a part-time developer.
attacks.evidence: "Ghost 5.x (MIT licensed) self-hosted via the official Docker image"

attacks.claim: Sign-in and receipt email over the new SMTP path has no test step before cutover, so a failure would first surface to paying members.
attacks.evidence: "Transactional mail (sign-in links, receipts) goes over plain SMTP and is provider-independent."; ABSENT: pre-cutover test

attacks.claim: Editor training is scheduled in week 3 with no readiness check before the first Ghost send, leaving about two days to fix problems.
attacks.evidence: "editor training" in week 3; "giving 2 days to fix issues"

attacks.claim: Only the CSV/JSON export round-trip is tested. The full MySQL dump restore is never exercised, so the disaster-recovery claim is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "we restore one export into a scratch Ghost instance in week 2"

attacks.claim: The 200/301 crawl checks status codes only. A layout or rendering regression on the top 2,000 URLs would pass the cutover gate.
attacks.evidence: "A crawl of the 2,000 most-visited URLs from analytics must return 200/301 before cutover."

attacks.claim: Neither the theme port nor the newsletter templates have a stated accessibility check for contrast, keyboard access, or screen-reader structure.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility review in theme or template scope

attacks.claim: Success measures cover only internal outage and labour metrics. No reader outcome measure, such as retention or open rate, confirms the migration helps subscribers.
attacks.evidence: "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter."; ABSENT: reader outcome metrics

attacks.claim: The outage root cause is asserted without logs or incident evidence, and the zero-outage target has no baseline or instrumentation.
attacks.evidence: "MailPoet's WP-cron sending competes with site traffic on the same PHP workers."; "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter."

attacks.claim: The shortcode repair script is unversioned and not re-runnable, so the 41-post fix cannot be reproduced if the dry run is repeated.
attacks.evidence: "41 posts with embedded shortcodes fixed by script"
